Factories and brick kilns cause the air to look like fog but really is pollution.l  There were about 10,000 people there that day to tour the Taj Mahal.  People who look like obvious foreigners are required to buy the VIP pass.  It's well worth it to pay the extra for a VIP pass because you go through a special faster line with fewer people to get into the grounds and later to get into the Taj Mahal itself. While it was pretty, I can't say that it was enjoyable because of all the people.  Once you are inside the Taj Mahal the VIP pass doesn't do anything for you. Review_Text: There probably isn't anything left to write about with respect to visiting the Taj Mahal.  For what it is worth, our trip started early in the day (7am) to beat the crowds.  The Taj already had plenty of visitors as we arrived.  A guide is essential to get the most from the visit - if you don't want one come with a guide book as finding one on site is not easy (although you can haggle outside for one).  There are quiet areas from which to view the Taj - most people stick to the central concourse to get pictures square on to the main building - you can get some equally good pictures off to the side where there are plenty of empty benches to sit on.  Worth taking the time to sit away from the crowds and just admire the building.  You need 'over-shoes' to go into the main building concourse and inside the tomb itself - our tour provided these (disposable) and worth having before entering.  There is security on entry and strict rules about what you can bring on site (no chewing gum, foodstuffs etc) - my advise is travel light for your visit.

We visited two of Wildlife SOS’s sanctuaries whilst staying in Agra. These are not zoos but have been created to provide sanctuary to abused elephants and sloth bears. The aim of the charity, in addition to caring for these beautiful creatures which have endured horrific cruelty at the hands of humans, is to educate people including tourists about the horrors of elephant domestication and bear dancing and ultimately end these cruel practices - including elephant rides for tourists. Thankfully bear dancing is now illegal in India but the bears are still being poached in the wild. Elephant domestication is still not illegal in India but the charity is committed to its goal of ending it. The staff were so incredibly knowledgeable and the respect and love they exhibit towards the animals they care for was inspiring. We were shown around the bear sanctuary by Ruman and the elephant sanctuary by Himanshu both of whose knowledge about wildlife was amazing. We felt so grateful to the staff and inspired by the wonderful work Wildlife SOS are doing. In addition to providing sanctuary to these creatures and spreading their educational message the charity also helps the people who depend on the exploitation of these animals to find other ways of earning their livelihood often in the case of the beautiful craft work which you can buy in the shop directly helps spread Wildlife SOS’s message further.

I debated about giving this 3 or 4 circles and decided on four. Seeing Gaudi's work was a main draw for me in visiting Barcelona. Getting to the Park was not as easy as getting to other major sites in Barcelona. We took the metro to the Park Guell stop, but then had to walk about 10-15 minutes (some uphill a bit) to reach the park entrance. Luckily we were able to enter even though we arrived past our pre-purchased ticket window time. The park has a nice walking path, but the main highlights, especially with the mosaic tile benches, are overrun with people. Plus the pictures I had seen prior to visiting made it seem like it would be a lot more colorful than it ended up being. Dang photo editing making it look better than in person! There were a lot of people just hanging out on the benches blocking photo opportunities. It was kind of frustrating, but then you remember they are benches and made for sitting... We went into one of the buildings which had some signs, pictures and videos about the park project and how it ended up being what it is today. Visiting that first might be smart to have a better understanding of the park as a whole. Looking back, I'm glad we went but I wouldn't recommend putting this at the top of your must-see list while in Barcelona.

But you’ll know it if you’re in it because much of the architecture will have that medieval feel to it. There are statues and basilicas and so many cool, narrow alleys. Be aware that it is a popular area for tourists, so it will always be crowded. And because the streets are narrow that could lead to some frustration. We went in January so it wasn’t too bad but I can imagine a more popular month being a little harder to get around. Expect a lot of graffiti. Like Rome, it seems to be everywhere. Every single roll down metal store front is a canvas (not just in this quarter, but throughout Barcelona) to the point that I wonder if many of these are commissioned.

So I can now say I’ve been in the tallest building in the world. You have two options. You can go up to the 124th/125th floors (costs about £30) or choose to go up to the 148th floor (cost about £80). We decided on the later. For this price you also get a fast pass (so not much queuing) and refreshments. We went during Ramadan, so refreshments weren’t available. If you do decide to go to the 148th floor, you can then come down and look at the views from the 124th/125th floors. We did this and must admit, you can’t tell any difference from looking down from the 124th compared to the 148th. The views are exactly the same. It’s like looking out of a plane window at 10,000ft compared to 15,000ft, you wouldn’t know the difference unless someone told you what height you were flying at. All you can see is, it’s a long way down to the ground. And because of this, I would only recommend going to the 124th/125th floors, this way you will also save yourselves a lot of money.

Even my kids (teens), who are not art fans and argued all the way, liked it very much. Just few words on place history: this was a low class neighborhood with small businesses and abandoned warehouses, a Miami area you don't want to visit with a high crime rate. Mr. Goldman, entrepreneur, investment building contractor and a visionary bought this land and gave it for free for many international artists to express themselves and have their opportunity. This art heaven is what they made. The place consists of six ex warehouses, whose exteriors serve as giant canvases for extrodinary huge murals, while the interior is full of art pieces: paintings, art sculpture masterpieces, artistic every day objects, etc....which are sold at 3 to 6 figures price tags.
